rationale: Both responses correctly identify the central point: MoE separates stored from active parameters, saving compute but not memory, so quality per byte favors dense when memory binds. Both also repeat the same factual error, giving Mixtral 8x7B about 129B total parameters when the real figure is about 47B. Both assert, with limited support, that MoE is more fragile under quantization. A is more actionable and insightful for a practitioner. It distinguishes the fits-in-memory and paged-experts latency regimes, and uses Qwen3-30B-A3B as a real case where MoE wins on a 32 GB machine. It gives memory-tier recommendations and practical tips: keep the router and attention at higher precision, test tool-calling under quantization, and measure p95 TTFT on real prompts. B is cleaner and well reasoned. It separates prefill and decode and gives a crisp three-condition checklist for choosing MoE. However, it stays more generic and offers no concrete examples of when MoE is the right local choice. A has some speculative details, such as hallucinated routing and the consistency-over-speed example, but overall it offers more depth and decision-relevant guidance.
